summary: Created an 8-phase plan for the five extension-manifest quick-fix items. Phase 1 captures a verify-deploy.sh --findings baseline; phases 2-7 apply one item each (keyword_overrides reshape, mcpServers casing, 3MB pptx deletion, literature->filetypes dependency drop, orphaned mcp_servers resolution, empty-stub sweep); phase 8 gates on a findings subset-diff against the baseline. Waves keep same-file phases serialized so no two parallel phases touch one manifest.
decisions_made: Adopted the research's item-5 resolution verbatim: founder/filetypes/memory get settings-fragment.json + merge_targets.settings; present's mcp_servers.superdoc block is deleted.

Sweep all 16 empty hooks:{} stubs (including core, literature, epidemiology) rather than reconstructing the review's exclusion arithmetic to hit a literal 13; live enumeration is the work list, not the plan's counts.

Keep the top-level mcp_servers block in founder/filetypes/memory manifests: the extension picker previewer reads manifest.mcp_servers for display, so the fragment is the merge path rather than a replacement for that display.
settings-fragment.json is routed via merge_targets.settings only, never via provides.* (verified against lean and nix), so no provides schema change is in scope.
Phase 1 baseline is a hard gate: if verify-deploy.sh is not already clean, stop before any edit rather than absorbing a pre-existing failure into the 'no new findings' bar.
